AUTHOR: Olsvik, E; Trinh, CMD; Knausgård, KM; Wiklund, A; Sordalen, TK; Kleiven, AR; Jiao, L; Goodwin, M
TITLE: Biometric Fish Classification of Temperate Species Using Convolutional Neural Network with Squeeze-and-Excitation
VENUE: ADVANCES AND TRENDS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE: FROM THEORY TO PRACTICE
SPECIES: Corkwing wrasse (male/female), pollack, coalfish (post-training); 23 F4K species pre-training
DATA: Own IMR temperate dataset (GoPro reef cameras + stereo-BRUV); Fish4Knowledge for pre-training
V_EV: Sec 2.1: 'cameras were deployed between 8 and 35 meters'; 'higher image noise (visibility, background, resolution)' - depth reported, visibility qualitative only, no stratified results
D_EV: Sec 3.1: 'the applicable data set was divided into 70% training images, 15% validation images and 15% testing images'
R_EV: Sec 3.1: post-training tested on 'a subset of 155 images of the same classes were reserved for testing' from the same temperate dataset
C_EV: Sec 2.2: 'The final layer, softmax, applies a classifier function to obtain the probability distribution for each class per input image' - no threshold/reject
E_EV: Table 3: 'Average testing accuracy over 10 runs and time per epoch on post-training' - accuracy only
ARCH: CNN-SENet (custom CNN with Squeeze-and-Excitation); baselines Inception-V3, ResNet-50, Inception-ResNet-V2
NOTE: Full text is arXiv version of proceedings paper. Split unit not stated beyond image counts drawn from videos; authors note some S. melops males 'tracked and captured by camera multiple times' (possible leakage, not discussed as such). Pre-trained on Fish4Knowledge (train/val/test 19149/4126/4126). V3 coded NR although 'sun exposure' variation mentioned qualitatively.
